activity.notes: Isoroku Yamamoto (1884–1943), Combined Fleet commander-in-chief from 1939, directed Japanese naval strategy and developed the 1941 Pearl Harbor attack plan. The representative 1941 military Activity is planning and overall command, not physical tactical command of the carrier strike force, which was led by Chūichi Nagumo; he also directed naval strategy in subsequent campaigns including the failed Midway operation. Pearl Harbor precipitated the United States' entry into the Pacific War. Yamamoto was killed by U.S. aircraft in April 1943. This is documentation of his wartime role, not praise or an endorsement of the attack.
